ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: To calculate $\tan 15^\circ$, as shown in the figure, in $\text{Rt}\triangle ABC$, $\angle C=90^\circ$, $\angle ABC=30^\circ$. Extend $CB$ to $D$, so that $BD=AB$, and connect $AD$, then $\angle D=15^\circ$. Thus, $\tan 15^\circ =\frac{AC}{CD}=\frac{1}{2+\sqrt{3}}=\frac{2-\sqrt{3}}{(2+\sqrt{3})(2-\sqrt{3})}=2-\sqrt{3}$. Following this method, what is the value of $\tan 22.5^\circ$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, in the isosceles right-angled $\triangle ABC$, $\angle C=90^\circ$. Extend $CB$ to point $D$ such that $AB=BD$, then $\angle BAD=\angle D$.\\
$\because \angle ABC=45^\circ$,\\
$\therefore 45^\circ=\angle BAD+\angle D=2\angle D$,\\
$\therefore \angle D=22.5^\circ$,\\
Let $AC=1$, then $BC=1$, $AB=\sqrt{2}AC=\sqrt{2}$,\\
$\therefore CD=CB+BD=CB+AB=1+\sqrt{2}$,\\
$\therefore \tan 22.5^\circ=\tan D=\frac{AC}{CD}=\frac{1}{1+\sqrt{2}}=\frac{1-\sqrt{2}}{(1+\sqrt{2})(1-\sqrt{2})}=\boxed{\sqrt{2}-1}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, A is at the upper left, C is at the lower left, AC is vertical, and C, B, D are on the same horizontal straight line; connect A to B and D respectively, a right angle is marked at C, 30° is marked at B, and 15° is marked at D, showing the method of extending CB to D and using the isosceles triangle construction with AB=BD to construct a half angle. Reasoning: Imitate the method in the figure to find tan22.5°. Take Rt△ABC as an isosceles right triangle, making ∠C=90° and ∠ABC=45°. Extend CB to D, make BD=AB, and connect AD. Because AB=BD, △ABD is an isosceles triangle, so ∠BAD=∠D. Also because C, B, D are collinear, in △ABD there is ∠BAD+∠D=∠ABC=45°, so 2∠D=45°, that is, ∠D=22.5°. Let AC=BC=1, then AB=√2. Since BD=AB=√2, CD=CB+BD=1+√2. In Rt△ACD, tan22.5°=tan∠D=AC/CD=1/(1+√2). Rationalizing gives 1/(1+√2)=√2−1.
